newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO SEES COPPER SUPPLY DEFICITS IN 97,98.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO SEES COPPER SUPPLY DEFICITS IN 97,98.

text.p: Asarco Inc now expects world copper supply deficits this year and next, followed by a small surplus in 1999 and another deficit in 2000, chief executive Richard Osborne said Friday.

"This is a far cry from the wave of (supply) surpluses" others are projecting, he told Asarco's quarterly analysts' meeting, adding the estimate uses a "relatively low growth rate in Western (World copper) consumption.
Asarco sees Western consumption of 12.2 million short tons this year, up 3.5 percent from 1996, followed by growth of 3.4 percent next year and 3.0 percent in 1999 and 2000, he said.
